title: Configuration
description: Configure Soup CLI with a single YAML file. Set base model, training task, LoRA params, and data paths via Pydantic v2 schema. Unknown keys, since v0.76.0 dozens of combinations that loaded on v0.75, since v0.76.1 a soup.yaml over 1 MiB or nested deeper than 100 levels, and since v0.77.0 the staged fields and deprecated config values v0.76 warned about are refused when the config loads; soup doctor --config reports the refusal before you train.

headings.title: More keys, and where each is documented

blocks.html:
Configuration

Soup uses a single YAML config file for all settings. Run soup init to generate one. Every key with its type, default and bounds is also listed in upstream's generated docs/config-reference.md at v0.77.0, which since v0.77.0 is rendered from the schema at each release; this page explains the keys that need explaining, and Settings refused at load lists what the load refuses.

Reproducibility and full fine-tuning (v0.73.0)

Two training keys landed in v0.73.0. Both are config keys, not CLI flags.

blocks.code:
training:
  seed: 1234           # weight init of new params, data order, dropout
  data_seed: 7         # optional: vary data order while holding init fixed
  quantization: none   # required with r: 0, because the default (4bit) is refused
  lora:
    r: 0               # 0 means no adapter: full fine-tuning, dense checkpoint

blocks.html:
seed and data_seed are the first seed knobs in the project's history: before this every run trained at seed 42 with no way to change it, so "run this twice with a different seed" was impossible. Both default to unset rather than to 42, deliberately, because an unset seed has to keep reproducing two different historical defaults (the trainer's 42 and the multipack sampler's 0) and a plain 42 would have silently re-ordered every existing multipack run. A boolean is refused by name, since seed: true would otherwise become seed 1.

The honest scope, and it widened in v0.73.1: the seed reaches the trainer arguments in every wrapper now, applied before the model loads, so setting it on a DPO run is real. It reached one wrapper of eighteen when it shipped in v0.73.0, which is what the original note here described. On a streamed run it additionally seeds the adapter initialisation for all five streaming tasks, which is why a streamed run is bit-reproducible from a seed while a resident 4-bit one still is not.

lora.r: 0 selects full fine-tuning on task: sft and, since v0.75.0, task: embedding: no adapter is built, and the run writes a dense checkpoint rather than a LoRA. On any other task the gate does not apply at all, and that is worth knowing before you rely on it: classifier, reranker, cross_encoder and asr gate LoRA behind their own flag and ignore the rank entirely, while the remaining tasks hand the 0 straight to PEFT, which rejects it with its own message about a positive integer rather than Soup's named one. Since v0.77.0 task: pretrain refuses lora.r: 0 at load by name, because its trainer always attaches an adapter, unless lisa_enabled: true, which attaches none (on sft and embedding the full fine-tuning gate below still refuses rank 0 with LISA); and the MLX preference tasks (dpo, orpo, simpo, kto on backend: mlx) require lora.r of 1 or more. LLaMA Pro block expansion (expand_layers) needs lora.r: 0 since v0.77.0. Rank 0 was chosen because three parts of the codebase already read it as "no adapter" and because r: 0 used to crash, so no config that worked before changes meaning. It is refused with a named message alongside a non-transformers backend, a non-text modality, any quantisation (the default counts: quantization is 4bit unless you set it, which is why the block above sets none), Spectrum, LISA, layer streaming, or any LoRA-shaped option, and it refuses rather than running a no-op if your freeze settings leave nothing trainable.

Config Structure

blocks.code:
base: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct   # HuggingFace model ID (required)
task: sft                                   # Training task
# backend: unsloth                          # 2-5x faster (pip install "soup-cli[fast]")
# modality: text                            # text, vision, or audio

data:
  train: ./data/train.jsonl                 # Local file, remote URI or Hub dataset name
  format: alpaca                            # Data format (auto-detected if omitted)
  val_split: 0.1                            # Validation split ratio (evaluated each epoch since v0.76.0, except on grpo, ppo and online_dpo)
  max_length: 2048                          # Max sequence length (64-1048576)
  # image_dir: ./data/images               # For vision modality
  # audio_dir: ./data/audio                # For audio modality

training:
  epochs: 3
  lr: 2e-5
  batch_size: auto                          # auto or integer
  quantization: 4bit                        # the default; also none, 8bit, gptq, awq, hqq:Nbit, ...
  # weight_decay: 0.01                      # default 0.01
  # max_grad_norm: 1.0                      # gradient clipping, default 1.0
  # logging_steps: 10                       # log metrics every N steps
  # save_steps: 100                         # checkpoint every N steps
  # warmup_ratio: 0.03                      # 0.0-0.5, default 0.03
  # scheduler: cosine                       # LR scheduler
  # quantization_aware: fp8               # fp8 or quest; true (int8 QAT) is refused since v0.76.0
  # optimizer: adamw_8bit
  # gradient_checkpointing: true            # default false; since v0.77.0 the value reaches every trainer (see below)
  # stream_layers: false                   # Train or align a model bigger than VRAM (v0.72, BETA)
  # stream_source: auto                    # auto | ram | disk
  # stream_buffers: 2                      # 2-8
  # stream_pin: false                      # v0.74.0: force the pageable store
  # stream_read_ahead: 2                   # v0.76.0, disk tier only: 1-8
  lora:
    r: 64
    alpha: 16
    dropout: 0.05
    # target_modules: auto                 # Auto-detected per model
    # use_dora: false                      # Weight-decomposed LoRA

output: ./output

blocks.html:
Defaults worth knowing

These are the values a key takes when you leave it out. The quantization default is the one that surprises people: quantization is 4bit unless you set it, so a config that does not mention it trains a QLoRA. The exception is eight tasks whose trainer never quantizes the base: on those an unset value resolves to none (see Keys a task ignores).

KeyDefaultBound or note
epochs3at least 1
lr2e-5
batch_sizeautoauto or an integer
gradient_accumulation_steps4at least 1
quantization4bitlora.r: 0 (full fine-tuning) refuses it, so set none. Unset resolves to none on distill, classifier, reranker, cross_encoder, prm, moe_lora_routing, unlearn and asr
optimizeradamw_torch
schedulercosinea free string: the config does not check the name, it is passed to the trainer
weight_decay0.010 or more
max_grad_norm1.0greater than 0
warmup_ratio0.030.0 to 0.5
logging_steps10
save_steps100
gradient_checkpointingfalseSince v0.77.0 the value reaches the trainer. With the default false, grpo, ipo, bco, reward_model and online_dpo train with checkpointing off (TRL's own default used to apply), and on backend: unsloth false now disables Unsloth's checkpointing. Set true to keep the memory you had. distill, classifier, reranker, cross_encoder, asr and unlearn now honour true too

What batch_size: auto does

auto starts from a static estimate built from the model size, sequence length, quantization and LoRA rank. On a CUDA card the SFT trainer alone then refines it with a real probe, one forward and backward at each candidate size, starting at the estimate, halving when it runs out of memory and doubling while it fits, never above four times the estimate (training.auto_batch_size_strategy chooses auto, the default, probe or static; see OOM-probe auto batch size). The answer is cached per base model, sequence length, quantization, LoRA rank and GPU. Every other task, every CPU run and static use the static estimate unchanged. task: kto floors the estimate at 2, because a KTO config with batch_size: 1 is refused (below).

It errs high when the whole model trains. The estimate charges trainable-parameter memory as a small share of the model, at most 5% and derived from the LoRA rank, and charges none for lora.r: 0. The probe never takes an optimizer step, so it does not see the optimizer state either, which for AdamW is two extra values for every trainable parameter. With lora.r: 0 or with unfrozen_parameters (Spectrum), set batch_size explicitly, or start low and raise it. LISA (lisa_enabled) is a separate case: the probe also runs while every layer is still trainable, so its gradient figure is not LISA's either, and which way it errs was not measured. Set batch_size explicitly there as well.

Size and nesting limits (v0.76.1)

Since v0.76.1 every YAML file Soup reads goes through one loader. Nesting is limited to 100 levels, and the document's top-level mapping counts as the first, so 99 levels of brackets under a top-level key is the deepest structure that loads. Expansion is limited to one node per source byte plus 10,000 for anchors, aliases and merge keys, with merge keys chained at most 100 levels. Each reader keeps its own size cap:

What is readSize cap
A training config (soup.yaml), and the readers that had no cap before1 MiB
Recipes, soup export --quant-config files, RA-DIT configs and sweep files256 KiB
Agent specs5 MiB
Can manifests16 MiB
README front matter64 KiB
The config read by soup ship4 MiB

A soup.yaml that is over a limit, cannot be read or is not valid YAML stops the load with one line naming the file and the problem, for example Config file soup.yaml is larger than 1048576 bytes; refusing or Config file soup.yaml is not valid YAML: expected ',' or ']', but got '<stream end>' (line 6, column 1). soup train exits 1 and soup doctor --config exits 2. The other readers report through their own handlers: soup plan and soup apply exit 2 on a limit and 1 on a syntax error, soup eval gate exits 3 on a suite over a limit and 1 on a syntax error (soup train --gate exits 1 on either), and soup ship --config exits 3. How a config loads lists the messages the training-config loader prints.

These are new refusals: a config that loaded on v0.76.0 can stop loading, so run soup doctor --config soup.yaml first, as for an upgrade to v0.76.0. A hand-written config is kilobytes and nests a few levels.

Layer streaming keys

These turn on layer streaming, which trains a model larger than your VRAM by keeping the frozen base out of the card entirely. They are config keys, not CLI flags: there is deliberately no --stream-layers.

KeyValuesDefaultNotes
stream_layerstrue / falsefalseBETA. Only enable it if the model does not fit resident; streaming trades time for memory
stream_sourceauto / ram / diskautoauto takes RAM when the base fits and falls back to an NVMe tier; ram refuses instead of falling back; disk forces NVMe
stream_buffers2 to 82VRAM buffers in the pool. 2 is double-buffering; 1 cannot overlap load with compute, so it is refused
stream_read_ahead1 to 82v0.76.0. Disk tier only: how many layers the background reader stages. One slot is always the layer in use, so N stages N-1 ahead. Each level costs one more layer of host staging memory. A non-default value beside stream_source: ram is refused, because the RAM tier reads nothing ahead. See The disk tier
stream_vram_probetrue / falsefalsev0.73.1. Decide the fit by measuring one real forward and backward at your shape, instead of predicting it. task: sft only. Costs 1 to 5 seconds, and cannot overrule a prediction more than 4x over budget
stream_disk_kindnvme / ssd / hdd(unset)v0.73.3. Override the detected media type behind the disk tier. nvme forces the tier on, ssd and hdd force it off. The override prints beside what was actually detected, and deliberately carries no measured rate, so a later refusal can never cite a reading you overrode
stream_vram_overridebytes(unset)v0.73.1. Replaces the free-VRAM figure the pre-flight checks against, in either direction. It changes the yardstick, not the check: an override below real free VRAM still refuses a config that would otherwise fit
stream_pintrue / false(unset)v0.74.0. Force the RAM store pageable or page-locked instead of letting Soup decide. false prints the throughput it costs rather than absorbing it silently; true refuses on a CUDA box that cannot page-lock, naming the size rather than a ceiling nobody probed: the RAM store on the RAM tier and, since v0.76.0, the background reader's host staging on the disk tier (it was announced-and-proceeds there before). With no CUDA device there is nothing to page-lock, and it is announced and the run proceeds on a pageable CPU source
stream_ngram_sourceauto / ram / diskautov0.74.0. Where Qwen4-Exp's external N-gram table is read from. Read-only, and only meaningful for that family
stream_recomputeon / off / autoonv0.77.0. on is the shipped checkpoint recompute; off keeps the streamed layers' activations instead of recomputing them in the backward (more VRAM); auto keeps them for as many layers as fit, on the RAM tier only. task: sft only, and refused beside activation_offloading. See Layer streaming
stream_loss_chunk16 to 8192 tokens(unset)v0.77.0. Computes the output head and the loss in token chunks, so the logits term no longer grows with data.max_length. Upstream: it matches the unchunked step within 1e-5 of the largest value, not bit for bit, and it has not been measured on a GPU. task: sft only; refused with data.format: raft and beside use_cut_ce
stream_nf4_scale_cachetrue / falsefalsev0.77.0. Keeps the expanded NF4 block scales on the GPU after first use instead of re-expanding them; bit-identical results, at a cost of 4 bytes of VRAM per 64-element block. Needs quantization: 4bit with double quantization
stream_expert_layoutfused / per_expertfusedv0.77.0. per_expert streams a DeepSeek-V3-family MoE one routed expert at a time; refused with moe_lora, and on other architectures at setup. See Streaming a Mixture-of-Experts base

Setting any of these while stream_layers is false is refused, because the knobs would silently do nothing; the message names only the keys you set. Streaming also reads one environment variable for the disk tier, SOUP_LAYER_STREAM_STRIPE_DIRS (see Environment variables).

A key the schema does not declare is no longer silently dropped (v0.74.0). Until then none of the config models overrode the library default of ignoring undeclared keys, so a typo validated clean and was discarded: training.quantizaton: none trained 4-bit, training.gradient_checkpoint: true did no checkpointing, data.max_len: 512 truncated at 2048, and soup train --dry-run printed "Config valid. Ready to train!" Loading a config now walks the whole model tree and reports every key it cannot place in one report, naming the field you probably meant. Since v0.75.0 the load is refused. soup train exits 1 before the training stack is imported, and the API and Web UI loader raises ValueError with the same text. Nothing is defaulted and nothing is substituted; the message says Refused. rather than Not applied., which would have read as if the run went ahead without the key, and the scan stops at 100 findings and says so. Two things are worth knowing. A config that must stay loadable on v0.74 as well needs the key removed, not renamed, because v0.74 warns and ignores it while v0.75 refuses it, and neither applies it. And soup plan and soup apply refuse an unknown key the same way (exit 1), but they run only that check and not the schema validators, so soup plan writes a plan for a config that soup doctor --config refuses (see Pre-flight tooling). soup sweep is stricter, because a swept parameter that matches nothing produces a grid of identical arms and a meaningless winner: it exits 1 before the first arm.

That refusal covers keys the schema does not know. A key the schema declares and no code reads is a different case, and since v0.77.0 it falls into two groups (v0.76.0 had a third, the fields that only warned).

  1. Refused at load. Dozens of combinations that loaded on v0.75 were refused in v0.76.0 with a message that names the field and what to change; on v0.75 some of them were ignored and some failed later. Examples: use_liger or use_flash_attn on a task that is not sft or tts, rope_scaling_type on a task that does not rescale RoPE, freeze_layers on dpo, quantization_aware: true, optimizer: muon on the transformers backend. Since v0.77.0 the 31 staged fields (validated, read by nothing) stop the load when set away from their default, each with a line ending refused as of v0.77. Delete the line.; so do data.remove_unused_columns: true and training.quantization: 4bit or 8bit (or load_in_8bit: true) on one of the eight tasks below that never quantize, and soup ab --beta exits 2. The 20 staged fields under training are long_context_grpo, vision_grpo, quantize_ref_model, grace_codebook, grace_codebook_size, grace_codebook_dim, lr_groups, early_stop_patience, citation_recall_threshold, forgetting_eval_steps, forgetting_benchmark, forgetting_stop, checkpoint_eval_steps, checkpoint_eval_metric, checkpoint_eval_tasks, checkpoint_keep_top, convergence_window, convergence_rel_tol, rl_checkpoint_include_ref_model and rl_checkpoint_include_rollout_buffer (the last two were never warned about: an explicit false loads, true is refused); the 11 under data are video_dir, video_fps, video_maxlen, image_min_pixels, image_max_pixels, image_resize_algorithm, split_thinking, eval_on_each_dataset, resize_vocab, extend_conversation and skip_prepare_dataset. Upstream also lists fifteen settings that v0.76 accepted without a word and never applied. Fourteen of them are refused since v0.77.0, among them training.use_mod on a route with no Mixture-of-Depths router, training.neftune_alpha on the tasks that never apply it and relora_steps on a loss with a frozen reference; the fifteenth, a KTO row with a malformed label, is dropped at data load with a reason. Settings refused at load groups the refusals. soup train exits 1 with Config validation error:; soup doctor --config exits 2 with the error and Config could not be loaded (see above).. Unknown keys are reported together, but a cross-field refusal prints only the first one it reaches, so fix that setting and run it again until it prints no error. Deleting the key is the fix, and for a staged field it changes no result.
  2. Still accepted in silence. A few keys are inert and are not in the staged table: the four parent switches forgetting_detection, checkpoint_intelligence, early_stop_on_regression and convergence_detection, plus forgetting_threshold (soup train prints a yellow Note: that they are set but not enforced) and warmup_auto. Upstream names no release for refusing them. The pages that document such a key say so, as "accepted by the schema, but nothing in v0.77.0 reads it". An unread key still takes part in the config hash that soup ship --config compares, so editing one makes earlier --evidence read as stale.

soup doctor --config also prints a small backend-support table. At v0.77.0 it covers eight combinations: sft on backend: mlx (12 settings), dpo, orpo, simpo and kto on backend: mlx (9 each), sft on backend: unsloth (none, because its unread settings are refused at load instead), and sft on the transformers backend with a vision or an audio modality (data.mask_history, one each). A setting refused at load never reaches the table. For every other task and backend it has no entry, so it prints None of the 0 setting(s) known to be unread on task=<t> backend=<b> is switched on in this config. whether or not the config has a problem. Read that line as "not reviewed", never as an all-clear. Since v0.77.0 the command no longer prints All checks passed! above a refused config.

stream_vram_probe and stream_vram_override are not interchangeable, and the difference is the point. stream_vram_probe is a measurement: it runs the step and reads the peak. stream_vram_override is an assertion you are making about how much VRAM is really available, which is what you need when the pre-flight cannot see the truth, as under a per-process memory cap in a hosted notebook.

Streaming also constrains keys you already set: quantization must be none or 4bit, batch_size must be a concrete number rather than auto, and task must be one of sft, dpo, orpo, simpo and kto. Streaming also refuses use_liger, use_flash_attn, quantization_aware, fp8_attention, nvfp4, rope_scaling_type, freeze_layers, freeze_ratio and relora_steps, and since v0.77.0 use_cut_ce, a non-default moe_aux_loss_coeff and use_mod. A LoRA target on lm_head or embed_tokens is no longer a config-load refusal: on an untied checkpoint any spelling of it is refused when the streamed model is built, and on a tied one it trains and saves. The full table is on Layer streaming. (kto needs batch_size of 2 or more; since v0.76.0 that holds for every KTO run, not only streamed ones.) Scaling a streaming run covers sizing, the VRAM pre-flight and the disk tier; Preference losses over streaming covers the four alignment tasks.

Keys a task ignores

Eight tasks load the base unquantized because their trainers never quantize it: distill, classifier, reranker, cross_encoder, prm, moe_lora_routing, unlearn and asr. On them:

  • An unset training.quantization resolves to none (it is 4bit everywhere else).
  • An explicit 4bit or 8bit (or load_in_8bit: true) is refused at load since v0.77.0: training.quantization: 4bit has no effect on task='distill': its trainer never quantises the base, so no run can honour it. Delete the line or set quantization: none. Refused as of Soup v0.77. (v0.76 loaded it with a warning and treated it as none.)
  • Any Quant Menu value such as gptq, and bnb_4bit_quant_storage, is refused at load.
  • task: prm also refuses a non-default training.lora block, because it fine-tunes every base parameter (lora.r: 0 loads).

expand_layers is refused unless the resolved quantization is none, on any task but sft and pretrain (since v0.76.0), and since v0.77.0 also with a LoRA rank (set lora.r: 0) and on task: pretrain. See Optimizer zoo.

How target_modules: auto is resolved

lora.target_modules: auto (the default) resolves in this order:

  1. Architectures that PEFT maps itself (llama, mistral, qwen2 and so on) use PEFT's own default.
  2. Architectures in Soup's table: the Qwen3.5 family and a set of Mixture-of-Experts models (qwen3_moe, deepseek_v3, deepseek_v4, glm4_moe, glm_moe_dsa, granitemoehybrid, kimi_k2, kimi_k25, gpt_oss, minimax_m2, minimax_m3_vl, mistral3). These target the attention projections; MiniMax-M3 and mistral3 use language-tower patterns, so the vision tower and projector stay unadapted. On the multi-head latent attention bases deepseek_v3 and kimi_k2, since v0.77.0 the query projections follow the checkpoint's q_lora_rank: an integer gives q_a_proj and q_b_proj, while q_lora_rank: null (Moonlight-16B-A3B, for example) gives a single q_proj, which is now targeted.
  3. Anything else is refused with training.lora.target_modules='auto' has no mapping for model_type=..., which asks for an explicit training.lora.target_modules list or, for a Mixture-of-Experts model, training.moe_lora: true. training.lora.target_parameters alone also suffices.

On granitemoehybrid only a few layers carry attention (4 of 40 on granite-4.0-h-tiny-base), so training prints a yellow Partial LoRA coverage: line. The notice ends by telling you to set training.lora.target_modules explicitly to include the other layers; Soup has not measured whether adapting a state-space projection trains well.

Templates

Soup includes 21 built-in templates:

blocks.code:
soup init --template chat          # Conversational fine-tune
soup init --template code          # Code generation
soup init --template medical       # Domain expert
soup init --template reasoning     # GRPO reasoning (DeepSeek-R1 style)
soup init --template vision        # Vision/multimodal fine-tune
soup init --template audio         # Audio/speech fine-tune
soup init --template kto           # KTO unpaired preference
soup init --template orpo          # ORPO (no reference model)
soup init --template simpo         # SimPO length-normalized preference
soup init --template ipo           # IPO regularized preference
soup init --template bco           # BCO binary classifier preference (v0.40)
soup init --template rlhf          # Full RLHF pipeline (SFT -> RM -> PPO)
soup init --template pretrain      # Continued pre-training on raw text
soup init --template moe           # MoE fine-tuning (ScatterMoE LoRA)
soup init --template longcontext   # 128k+ context fine-tuning
soup init --template embedding     # Sentence embedding fine-tuning
soup init --template tool-calling  # Function / tool-calling fine-tune (v0.25)

blocks.html: Four more are regulation-shaped (compliance pack, v0.71.35). Each is a valid training config on a license-clean Apache-2.0 base plus header comments naming that regime's exact commands, because Soup's compliance controls are CLI flags and commands rather than config keys:

blocks.code:
soup init --template hipaa         # Protected Health Information
soup init --template soc2          # SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria
soup init --template eu-ai-act     # EU AI Act Annex XI/XII
soup init --template sr-11-7       # SR 11-7 Model Risk Management

Task-Specific Config Keys

KeyTasksDescription

kto_betaKTOKTO beta parameter
orpo_betaORPOORPO beta parameter
simpo_gammaSimPOSimPO gamma parameter
cpo_alphaSimPOCPO alpha parameter
ipo_tauIPOIPO tau parameter
grpo_betaGRPO and its variantsKL coefficient, default 0.1. Since v0.76.0 gspo, dapo, dr_grpo, bnpo, two_sided and rft apply it too. 0 turns the KL penalty off (KL-free recipes) and is refused together with reward_hack_mitigation kl_control or pid_lagrangian

reward_fnGRPO, PPOReward function: accuracy, format, a path to a .py file, or a comma-separated ensemble. Since v0.77.0 judge_rank (GRPO only, not with modality: vision) scores each prompt's completions with an LLM judge; it needs grpo_judge (a judge URL, ollama://model, https://host/model or http://localhost:port/model, checked at load) and grpo_judge_max_calls, which has no default, and a run that could make more judge calls than that is refused after the data loads and before the model does. Prompts and completions are sent to the judge host you configure, and a retried request can mean up to three requests per counted call. No quality claim is made for it. See GRPO Plus

ppo_epochsPPOPPO training epochs
ppo_clip_ratioPPOPPO clip ratio
ppo_kl_penaltyPPOPPO KL penalty

Applied since v0.76.0 on sft, pretrain, embedding, dpo, kto, orpo, simpo, ipo, bco, grpo, ppo, online_dpo, reward_model, distill, and on classifier, reranker, cross_encoder and asr with their LoRA flag; through v0.75.2 only the first three read it. Refused on prm, moe_lora_routing, unlearn, backend: mlx, lora.use_vera, use_lorafa, use_galore and optimizer apollo_adamw, lomo, adalomo
use_galoreSFT, PretrainEnable GaLore optimizer
moe_loraEvery LoRA task but a fewTarget MoE expert layers. Read by sft, tts, pretrain, dpo, kto, orpo, simpo, ipo, bco, grpo, ppo, online_dpo, reward_model, embedding, distill, unlearn and, with classifier_lora: true, the classifier family. Refused on asr, prm, moe_lora_routing, SFT with vision or audio, and backend: unsloth. See Backends

use_ligerSFT, TTSLiger Kernel fused ops. Refused at load on any other task. Since v0.77.0, on a model type Liger has no kernels for, it says so and trains without Liger instead of reporting it enabled

use_ring_attentionnoneRing FlashAttention. Accepted, and checked before training (CUDA, two or more GPUs, ring-flash-attn installed, max_length of 8192 or more), but nothing in v0.77.0 applies it to the model
rope_scaling_typeSFT, TTS, PretrainRoPE scaling (linear, dynamic, yarn, llama3; longrope is refused). Applied before the model is built, on backend: transformers only (on SFT, the text path without stream_layers); refused at load on every other task, backend or path. See Long context
neftune_alphaSFT, TTS, DPO, IPO, KTO, ORPO, SimPO, BCO, PreferenceNEFTune noisy embeddings (0-50). Since v0.77.0 any value, 0.0 included, is refused at load on every other task (it was accepted and ignored)
packingSFT, PretrainSample packing for efficiency
curriculumSFTSort the training rows from short to long before training. The Trainer's default sampler is random, so the model does not see them in that order

curriculum_bucketsSFT; 13 tasks with curriculum_dynamicNumber of difficulty buckets (1-20, default 4). The static sort only prints it; the curriculum_dynamic callback reads it

loss_watchdog_thresholdSame as loss_watchdogLoss spike threshold (≤100)
loss_watchdog_patienceSame as loss_watchdogPatience before stopping (≤1000)
freeze_layersSFT, TTS (text, transformers, no streaming)Freeze bottom N layers (≤1000). Refused at load elsewhere. With LoRA, since v0.77.0 a frozen layer gets no adapter (through v0.76.1 the freeze did nothing on a LoRA run); it needs a list lora.target_modules, and a regex, all-linear, target_parameters, use_vera or a plan that freezes every layer is refused when the model is built

embedding_poolingEmbeddingPooling strategy

Since v0.76.0 a key set on a task, backend or path that never reads it is, for many keys, refused when the config loads rather than ignored. The refusal names the key, the task or backend, and what to do (Use task: sft, or remove the key); soup train, soup train --dry-run, soup sweep and soup doctor --config all refuse it, and deleting the key is the fix. For most of these keys a run that finished on v0.75 ignored the key and trained as if it were not there, and some of the rest stopped after the model had loaded. Three are different: for use_longlora, ebft_variant and quantization_aware: true the key was applied, wrongly, so a run that finished on v0.75 did not do what its config said (see Re-run this). The rows above say which keys: use_liger, use_flash_attn, auto_mixed_precision, freeze_layers, freeze_ratio, rope_scaling_type, moe_aux_loss_coeff, loss_watchdog and its two siblings, loraplus_lr_ratio, moe_lora, plus data.chat_template (below), expand_layers, backend: unsloth on the ten tasks with no unsloth setup, and data.add_new_tokens / new_special_tokens outside the eleven tasks that add tokens. v0.77.0 adds use_mod, neftune_alpha, relora_steps on a loss with a frozen reference, reasoning_effort and train_on_eot outside sft, tts and distill, citation_faithful on pretrain, moe_aux_loss_coeff on Unsloth or with streaming, quantization: 8bit on Unsloth, and lora.rank_pattern / alpha_pattern on MLX or Unsloth; soup sweep also refuses a --param that sets a staged field away from its default. A key not named there is still accepted and ignored by a task that does not read it, so check this column. use_ring_attention and use_galore still go through their pre-flight check first, on any task. That check can refuse a machine that lacks the package or, for use_galore, a config with quantization: 4bit or 8bit (the default is 4bit) or backend: unsloth, so use_galore: true on a DPO run with the default quantization stops the run before it starts. The curriculum_metric and curriculum_buckets rows are the other exception: with curriculum_dynamic: true (which requires curriculum: true) the dynamic-curriculum callback reads them on the 13 tasks that allow it (sft, pretrain, dpo, grpo, kto, orpo, simpo, ipo, bco, reward_model, embedding, ppo, preference). Check this column before assuming a key took effect on a DPO or GRPO run.

data.chat_template is applied since v0.76.0 by SFT and by the DPO, ORPO, SimPO, KTO, BCO, IPO, PPO, reward-model, GRPO and Online DPO trainers, for conversational data; through v0.75.2 only SFT applied it, so on the others the tokenizer's own template rendered the prompts. Tasks that never render chat (pretrain, embedding, classifier, reranker, cross_encoder, prm, asr, moe_lora_routing, unlearn) refuse the key at load, and since v0.77.0 so does backend: mlx, whose trainers render the model's shipped template only (#2051).

More keys, and where each is documented

These keys are all read by the code, and the defaults and refusals in this table are what the config loader does, checked against the schema at v0.77.0. Upstream's generated docs/config-reference.md at v0.77.0 lists every key.

KeyDefaultWhat it does
training.gptq_disable_exllamatrueLoad a GPTQ base without the exllama kernel, which silently breaks adapter training. Read only with quantization: gptq, so leave it on. See Quant menu

training.reward_hack_haltfalseStop a GRPO run on a HACK verdict from the reward-hack detector. Needs reward_hack_detector, which task: ppo refuses when the trainer is built. The config form of --reward-hack-halt
training.echo_trap_tokenizer_awarefalseScore echo traps on tokenizer ids instead of whitespace tokens. Needs echo_trap_enabled: true. The config form of --echo-trap-tokenizer-aware

training.reward_hack_*see the pageTwenty-two tunables for the mitigation controller, each refused while reward_hack_mitigation is off. Defaults and bounds: Reward-hack mitigation

Needs task: sft, backend: transformers, text, quantization none or 4bit, and lora.dropout: 0 (the default 0.05 is refused: training.fast_lora needs lora.dropout: 0; got 0.05). Upstream: verified on CPU (float32 and float64 against peft) only; the bf16/fp16, NF4 and streamed-CUDA checks have not been run, and no speedup is claimed. See Speed and memory

Two declared settings are the opposite case. data.remove_unused_columns defaults to false; an explicit true is refused at load since v0.77.0 (data.remove_unused_columns: true never had an effect ...; v0.76 loaded it with a warning and ignored it). The advise: block is accepted by the schema, but nothing in v0.77.0 reads it: its three keys goal, probe and record are used by nothing (soup advise takes them as flags only, see soup advise).
